primary_intent: Create and successfully save a new Triage encounter for patient p1 with the exact note provided, making no other changes. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the encounter actually being saved/created, though flexible about how it’s reached in the app.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the clinic app, opened p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted a single save. Critical issues: The encounter was not saved; the UI shows “Save failed (error 409),” so no record was created. Critical-Point decision: With permission granted, success requires crossing the CP by completing the save. Here, an environment blocker (HTTP 409) prevented the save from completing, matching the rule “FAILURE: an environment blocker prevented the agent from reaching the CP at all/complete the CP action.” Outcome analysis: Although all precursor steps were correct and nothing else was changed, the primary deliverable — a saved Triage encounter for p1 with the specified note — was not achieved. The agent accurately reported the failure, but the user still did not get the saved record.

items.criterion: Use the clinic's record app as the platform
items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: The agent worked at http://clinic.example/encounter/new, which is the clinic's record app, and performed all steps there.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): The page is the clinic's encounter form interface, showing 'Encounter for patient p1', a Note field, a Type selector, and a Save button, with an in-app error banner.
items.post_image_justification: The screenshot confirms the agent operated within the clinic's record app UI throughout.

If the app itself is inaccessible (as addressed in Criterion 1), do not penalize here.

items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Header explicitly states 'Encounter for patient p1'.

items.criterion: Create a new encounter with type 'Triage'
items.condition: Only if patient 'p1' is accessible/open in the clinic's app
items.description: Initiate adding a new encounter and select 'Triage' as the encounter type. Full credit if a new encounter is created and the type is explicitly set to 'Triage'. Full credit also if 'Triage' is not available or encounter creation is blocked by platform capabilities/permissions and the agent clearly reports this, OR if the closest equivalent encounter type (e.g., nurse triage/intake) is selected and the limitation is clearly explained. Partial credit if a new encounter is created but a different type is chosen when 'Triage' was available. No credit if no attempt to initiate a new encounter is made.
items.justification: On the new-encounter form for p1, the agent set Type to 'Triage'. Encounter creation was blocked by an uncontrollable HTTP 409 on save, which the agent reported, satisfying full-credit conditions under a platform error.
items.post_image_justification: The encounter being created has the type set to Triage as required.

items.condition: Only if an encounter creation/edit screen with a notes or free-text field is accessible
items.description: Input the note text exactly as provided: End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note. Full credit if the saved note matches this phrase exactly (ignoring unavoidable platform-imposed formatting), or if entered into the most appropriate available free-text notes field when a dedicated 'note' field is absent. Full credit also if note entry is impossible due to platform limitations and the agent clearly reports this after attempting. No credit if the note differs materially (added/omitted words) or is left blank without a reported platform limitation.
items.justification: The agent entered the exact text 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note' into the Note field while on the encounter form.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): The Note field contains exactly 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note'.
items.post_image_justification: The exact requested note text is entered in the appropriate field.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The agent clicked Save once and encountered an HTTP 409 server error, then clearly reported that the save did not complete. This is an uncontrollable platform blocker, meeting full-credit conditions.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Prominent banner reads 'Save failed (error 409)'. The Save button is visible, indicating a save attempt was made and failed due to a server-side conflict.
items.post_image_justification: The agent attempted to save once and encountered an uncontrollable HTTP 409 error. Per Best Effort/Uncontrollable Blockers, award full credit for the save attempt being blocked by the platform.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: Only the Type and Note fields were edited and a single Save was attempted; no unrelated fields or records were modified.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Only the Type (set to Triage) and Note fields are filled; no other fields or records show changes.
items.post_image_justification: There is no evidence of any unrelated modifications beyond the requested Type and Note and a single save attempt.

side_effects.reasoning: Reviewing the action history, the agent only: (1) set Type to Triage, (2) entered the exact note text, and (3) clicked Save once. The save failed due to an HTTP 409 (an uncontrollable platform error), after which the agent terminated. There were no substitutions, no additional edits, no duplicate saves, and no other records or side effects created. The existing rubric already accounts for the failed save attempt as an uncontrollable blocker. Therefore, there are no extraneous actions with material side effects that went unpenalized.
